title.narrative: Support to the Covenant of Mayors in Sub-Saharan Africa-Phase III (topup2023-2024)

description.narrative: This contract is a topup of the CTR ENERGY/2018/401471 to continue implementation in concordance with the AECID and AFD/EF components of the support to the CoM SSA Phase III. The goal is to strengthen climate resilience at continental level and support African climate action in line with the goals of the Paris Agreement.

title.narrative: Specific objective indicator 2:Number of cities newly implementing SEACAPs developed or improved by the Action

description.narrative: Specific objective indicator 2:Number of cities newly implementing SEACAPs developed or improved by the Action

comment.narrative: Indicator targets per logframe 1 to 3

During the reporting period 4 cities newly implemented developed SEACAPs by actively pursuing and working on priority actions identified within their SEACAPs Abuja Municipal Area Council AMAC Nigeria started implementing the Abuja Urban Lab focusing on enhancing the waste management governance system based on its SEACAP. Abuja Area Municipal Council AMAC Nigeria started implementing Urban Smart Energy USE based on the priority energy actions in its SEACAP. Nakuru Kenya started implementing Urban Smart Energy USE based on its priority actions in the energy plan of the SEACAP. Garoua Cameroon started implementing a public lighting project based on its SEACAP.

description.narrative: Specific objective indicator 3: Number of projects newly supported by the Action in the pipeline, or funded by, private sector, banks, and International Financial Institutions, by city or county and by volume of funding

comment.narrative: Indicator targets per logframe 1 to 3

By the end of the reporting period 2 climate adaptation projects have been taken up in the pipeline of private sector banks international financing institutions and governmentfunded organisations The Dallas ASILI project in Embu Kenya implemented by Kounkuey Design Initiative KDI1 was selected to be funded by SwedBio and People Powered Climate Democracy Accelerator with a volume of 10.00030.000 EUR currently under negotiation A flood resilience project in STMA Ghana originally supported by FCDO was submitted to the Africa Development Banks Adaptation Window and has received positive confirmation to move to the second phase of evaluation.

description.narrative: Output indicator 1.1 Involved functionaries of city administrations confirm that the knowledge obtained through participation in trainings/workshops was utilised for responsive urban planning and monitoring with increased knowledge and skills, for instance SEACAP development and monitoring

comment.narrative: Indicator targets per logframe 70 to 80

During the reporting period 4 participatory processes involving city staff were conducted. These processes included 8 meetings associated with the Dallas ASILI project the Mombasa City Lab the Abuja Urban Lab and the SekondiTakoradi Metropolitan Assembly SEACAP development process.Satisfaction surveys were administered directly after the sessions to collect initial feedback 94 considered the information provided largely relevant to the challenges within their specific contexts and applicable to their work. In the following period expost surveys will be distributed to evaluate if the acquired knowledge was indeed utilised.

comment.narrative: Indicator targets per logframe 1 to 4

4 official planning documents are currently under development expected to be reported in the next period as part of the following projects The SekondiTakoradi Metropolitan Assembly STMA SEACAP is under development and will be integrated into the STMAs Mediumterm Development Plan. For the Dallas ASILI project in Embu Kenya a Green Infrastructure Plan and designs for naturebased solutions NbS to be implemented at pilot sites within the informal settlement in Embu will be developed.12 The Mombasa City Lab in Kenya finalised flood risk and vulnerability assessment which will be included in a larger Mombasa Flood Response Strategy. The Abuja Urban Lab in Nigeria aims to enhance the waste management governance framework. The resulting documents will be defined and shared in the next reporting period

title.narrative: Output indicator 2 Number of relevant project documents that have been newly and/or developed with the support of the Action (by city and sector).

description.narrative: Output indicator 2 Number of relevant project documents that have been newly and/or developed with the support of the Action (by city and sector).

comment.narrative: Indicator targets per logframe 4 to 8

During the reporting period 2 relevant project documents were newly developed with the support of GIZ CoM SSA In SekondiTakoradi Metropolitan Assembly STMA Ghana a flood resilience project document was submitted to the Africa Development Bank. In Accra Ghana the Accra Biogas project document was submitted to Gap Fund.Further documents are under development or review pending official submission to financiers including those related to the Garoua public lighting project with newly revised tender documents and in Yaund where GIZ cooperates with the Fonds Spcial dEquipement et dIntervention Intercommunale FEICOM to support local authorities in preparing a pipeline of adaptation projects.Additionaly as part of the Urban Smart Energy USE implementation detailed technical and economic assessments of solar rooftop PV systems are currently being conducted and revised in 7 cities.

comment.narrative: Within the reporting period a total of 75 individual organisations have participated in at least one meeting as part of 4 participatory processes SO 2 including stakeholders from government private sector finance sector academia nongovernmental organization NGOs civil society organization CSOs international organisations international finance institutions the informal sector and the media.Additionally the upcoming report will also consider organisations participation in the Urban Smart Energy USE processes SO3.
